## Connect from Notion

In Notion, open **Settings** → **Notion MCP** and browse the directory. Select your AI assistant and follow its connection instructions.

## Manual setup

Use these instructions if you’re adding Notion as a custom MCP server or configuring a client directly. The remote server URL is `mcp.notion.com/mcp`.

> [card] [Codex](#codex-chatgpt)

> [card] [Claude Code](#claude-code)

> [card] [Cursor](#cursor)

> [card] [fx](#fx)

> [card] [Devin](#devin)

> [card] [VS Code](#vs-code-github-copilot)

> [card] [Antigravity](#antigravity)

### Codex (ChatGPT)

Codex is OpenAI's coding agent. See the [Codex MCP documentation](developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/) for more details.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Install the [Codex CLI](developers.openai.com/codex/cli) before running the commands below. If you see `command not found`, make sure `codex` is on your `PATH`.

...

**Step 2**

Enter **Notion** as the server name, select **HTTP** as the transport, and set the server URL to:

```
mcp.notion.com/mcp
```

...

## FAQs

> [accordion] Can I use Notion MCP without interactive authorization?
>
> Yes, on Business and Enterprise plans. A workspace owner can create an MCP token with **New MCP token** in the Developer portal. The MCP client sends the token as a bearer token to `mcp.notion.com/mcp`, with no browser sign-in.
>
> Enterprise workspaces that use SAML SSO can also use [enterprise-managed authorization](developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/enterprise-managed-authorization.md), where the company's identity provider grants access without a consent screen.

> [accordion] Which Notion plans can use Notion MCP?
>
> Notion MCP works on every plan. Some features depend on the workspace's plan:
>
> * **MCP tokens**: Business and Enterprise. Only workspace owners can create them.
> * **Enterprise-managed authorization**: Enterprise, with SAML SSO.
> * **Connected-source search** with `notion-connector-search`: Business or Enterprise with Notion AI.

...

> [accordion] What's the difference between Notion MCP and the open-source server?
>
> **Notion MCP** (`mcp.notion.com/mcp`) is our hosted, actively maintained server. It supports OAuth authorization and MCP tokens, and requires no infrastructure setup.
>
> The **open-source server** ([`notion-mcp-server`](github.com/makenotion/notion-mcp-server)) is no longer actively maintained. It authenticates with an integration token and requires you to manage your own connection and deployment.
>
> For most users, we recommend Notion MCP.

> [accordion] I'm building my own MCP client
>
> If you're integrating Notion MCP into your own application, see
> [Build an MCP client for Notion](developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/build-mcp-client.md) for OAuth
> and connection requirements.

# Authorization

Copy page Copy page

Authenticate Notion API requests with personal access tokens, internal connection tokens, or OAuth integration OAuth flows.

Copy page Copy page

##  What is authorization?

Authorization is the process of granting a connection or token access to Notion data. [Internal connections](developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/internal-connections) use a static credential called an internal connection API token, [personal access tokens](developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/personal-access-tokens) use a user-scoped static token, and [OAuth integrations](developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/oauth-integrations/overview) and [public integrations](developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/public-integrations/overview) use the [OAuth 2.0](oauth.net/2/) protocol.

##  Internal connection auth flow set-up

To use an internal connection, start by creating your connection in the [Developer portal](app.notion.com/developers/connections) . The internal connection will be associated with the workspace of your choice. You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

...

If you receive an error response from the API, check if the connection has been properly [added to the page](notion.com/help/add-and-manage-connections-with-the-api) . If this does not solve the problem, refer to our [Status codes](developers.notion.com/reference/status-codes) page for more information.

##  Personal access token authentication

Personal access tokens (PATs) are created directly by a Notion user in the [Developer portal](notion.so/developers) . There is no OAuth flow and no page picker. A PAT acts as the user who created it and uses that user’s permissions in the selected workspace. Use a PAT when a script, CLI workflow, Worker, or trusted tool should act as you. Use an internal connection for team-owned workspace automations, or an OAuth integration when each user needs to authorize your app. PATs use the same `Authorization` header as other credentials for the Notion API:

HTTP

```
GET  /v1/users/me  HTTP / 1.1 Authorization :  Bearer {PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN} Notion-Version :  2026-03-11
```

...

###  OAuth integration authorization overview

Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review is not required. As an overview, the authorization flow includes the following steps. Each step will be described in more detail below.

1

Navigate the user to the connection’s authorization URL. This URL is provided in the [Developer portal](app.notion.com/developers/connections) .

2

After the user selects which workspace pages to share, Notion redirects the user to the connection’s redirect URI and includes a `code` query parameter. The redirect URI is the one you specified in your [Developer portal](app.notion.com/developers/connections) .

3

Make a `POST` request to [create an access token](developers.notion.com/reference/create-a-token) , which exchanges the temporary `code` for an access token.

4

The Notion API responds with an access token and some additional information.

5

Store the access token for future API requests. View the [API reference docs](developers.notion.com/reference/intro) to learn about available endpoints.

###  Step 1 - Navigate the user to the connection’s authorization URL

After creating an OAuth integration in the [Developer portal](app.notion.com/developers/connections) , access the connection’s secrets in the **Configuration** tab. Similarly to the internal connections, these values should be protected and should never be included in source code or version control.

The Configuration tab provides the authorization URL for your OAuth integration

As an example, your `.env` file using these secrets could look like this:

...

HTTP

```
POST  /v1/oauth/token  HTTP / 1.1 Authorization :  Basic "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" Content-Type :  application/json { "grant_type" : "authorization_code" , "code" : "e202e8c9-0990-40af-855f-ff8f872b1ec6" ,  "redirect_uri" : "example.com/auth/notion/callback" }
```

# Authentication

> Learn how to authenticate your connection requests using bearer tokens.

Requests use the HTTP `Authorization` header to both authenticate and authorize operations. The Notion API accepts bearer tokens in this header. Bearer tokens are provided when you create an [internal connection](developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/internal-connections.md), create a [personal access token](developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/personal-access-tokens.md), or complete the OAuth flow for a [public connection](developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/public-integrations/overview).

results.title: Notion MCP – Connect Notion to your favorite AI tools
excerpts:
Notion MCP

Learn how to connect AI agents to your Notion workspace.
Suggest Edits
Connect your AI tools to Notion using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) , an open standard that lets AI assistants interact with your Notion workspace.

What is Notion MCP?

Notion MCP is our hosted server that gives AI tools secure access to your Notion workspace. It's designed to work seamlessly with popular AI assistants like ChatGPT, Cursor, and Claude.
High-level diagram of the MCP data flow, where Notion hosts both the MCP Server and the Public API, and your tools contain MCP clients that connect to the remote MCP server to access our tools. High-level diagram of the MCP data flow, where Notion hosts both the MCP Server and Notion's API , and your tools contain MCP clients that connect to the remote MCP server to access our tools.

Why use Notion MCP?

* Easy setup — Connect through simple OAuth, with one-click installation for supported AI tools
* Full workspace access — AI tools can read and write to your Notion pages just like you can
* Optimized for AI — Built specifically for AI agents with efficient data formatting

What can you do with Notion MCP?

* Create documentation — Generate PRDs, tech specs, and architecture docs from your research and project data
* Search and find answers — Let AI search across all your Notion and connected workspace content
* Manage tasks — Generate code snippets from task descriptions and update project status automatically

results.title: Integrating your own MCP client - Notion Docs
excerpts:
Build an MCP client for Notion

Connect your app or AI assistant to Notion MCP with OAuth 2.0, PKCE, and support for Notion’s tools.
Build an MCP client that connects to Notion MCP using OAuth 2.0 with PKCE.

Connection requirements

Notion provides a hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets MCP clients work with Notion workspaces. Use Streamable HTTP at mcp.notion.com/mcp. If your client uses the deprecated /sse endpoint, migrate to Streamable HTTP.
Your client must support:
* OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE
* Streamable HTTP (/mcp)
* Token refresh handling
* Secure credential storage

Prerequisites

[!NOTE]
This guide uses TypeScript/JavaScript examples, but the concepts apply to any programming language. The OAuth 2.0 flow, PKCE implementation, and MCP protocol are language-agnostic.
Required libraries (TypeScript/JavaScript):
npm install @modelcontextprotocol/client@2
npm install --save-dev @types/node

What is authorization?
Authorization is the process of granting a connection or token access to Notion data. Internal connections use a static API token, personal access tokens use a user-scoped static API token, and public connections use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

​

Internal connection auth flow set-up
To use an internal connection, start by creating your connection in the Developer portal . The internal connection will be associated with the workspace of your choice. You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.
Create a new connection from the Developer portal.
Once the connection is created, you can update its settings as needed under the Configuration tab and retrieve the installation access token in this tab. The installation access token will be used to authenticate REST API requests. The connection sends the same token in every API request.
Find the installation access token in the Configuration tab.

...

Making API requests with an internal connection
Any time your connection interacts with your workspace, include the installation access token in the Authorization header with every API request. However, if you are using Notion’s SDK for JavaScript to interact with the REST API, the token is set once when a client is initialized.
HTTP
GET  /v1/pages/b55c9c91-384d-452b-81db-d1ef79372b75  HTTP / 1.1 Authorization :  Bearer {INTEGRATION_TOKEN}
JavaScript
const  {  Client  }  =  require ( "@notionhq/client" ) // Initializing a client const  notion  =  new  Client ({ 	auth:  process . env . NOTION_TOKEN , }) const  getUsers  =  async  ()  =>  { 	const  listUsersResponse  =  await  notion . users .

...

Public connection authorization overview
Once your connection has been made public, you can update your connection code to use the public auth flow. As an overview, the authorization flow includes the following steps. Each step will be described in more detail below.
1
Navigate the user to the connection’s authorization URL. This URL is provided in the Developer portal .
2
After the user selects which workspace pages to share, Notion redirects the user to the connection’s redirect URI and includes a code query parameter. The redirect URI is the one you specified in your Developer portal .
3
Make a POST request to create an access token , which exchanges the temporary code for an access token.
4
The Notion API responds with an access token and some additional information.
5
Store the access token for future API requests. View the API reference docs to learn about available endpoints.

...

Step 3 - Send the code in a POST request to the Notion API
The connection needs to exchange the temporary code for an access_token . To set up this step, retrieve the code from the redirect URI. Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token . This endpoint is described in more detail in the API reference docs for creating a token . The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET , like so:
CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET
Find both of these values in the Developer portal . Note that in HTTP Basic Authentication , credentials are base64 encoded before being added to the Authorization header. The body of the request contains the following JSON-encoded fields:
* Field | Type | Description | Required

...

OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI ; // encode in base 64 const  encoded  =  btoa ( ` ${ clientId } : ${ clientSecret } ` ); const  response  =  await  fetch ( "api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token" , { 	method:  "POST" , 	headers:  { 	Accept:  "application/json" , 	"Content-Type" :  "application/json" , 	Authorization:  `Basic  ${ encoded } ` , }, 	body:  JSON . stringify ({ 		grant_type:  "authorization_code" , 		code:  "your-temporary-code" , 		redirect_uri:  redirectUri , 	}), }); ...

​

Step 4 - Notion responds with an access_token , refresh_token , and additional information
Notion responds to the request with an access_token , refresh_token , and additional information. The access_token will be used to authenticate subsequent Notion REST API requests. The refresh_token will be used to refresh the access token, which generates a new access_token . The response contains the following JSON-encoded fields:

sources.title: Notion API quickstart
sources.trimmed:
Build tools and automations that create pages, organize data, and share feedback in Notion. This guide walks you through creating your first page with the API. You need a Notion account and a terminal.

## Step 1: Get a personal access token

A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow.

1

Open Personal access tokens in the Developer portal.

2

Select **New token**.

3

Enter a name, select the **Notion API** capability, and then select **Create token**. If a workspace picker appears, select a workspace first.

4

Copy the token and save it somewhere secure. You won’t be able to see it again.

**Don’t see the option to create a token?**On Business and Enterprise plans, PAT creation is restricted by default. Ask a workspace owner to enable it in **Settings → Connections**.See Who can create PATs.

Set the token as an environment variable so you can use it in the examples below. Set it again if you open a new terminal. Keep the token out of browser code and public repositories.

```
export NOTION_API_KEY=ntn_...
```

```
$env:NOTION_API_KEY = "ntn_..."
```

## Step 2: Create a page

Make a POST request to the Create a page endpoint with markdown content. The API creates a private page in your workspace, using the `# heading` as the page title automatically.

```
curl -X POST https://api.notion.com/v1/pages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTION_API_KEY" \
  -H "Notion-Version: 2026-03-11" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "icon": { "emoji": "🚀" },
    "markdown": "# Hello from the API\n\n## Welcome\n\nThis page was created with the Notion API. You just made your first request!\n\n- Read the [API reference](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro)\n- Explore [examples](https://developers.notion.com/page/examples)"
  }'
```

```
POST https://api.notion.com/v1/pages
Authorization: Bearer {PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json
Notion-Version: 2026-03-11

{
  "icon": { "emoji": "🚀" },
  "markdown": "# Hello from the API\n\n## Welcome\n\nThis page was created with the Notion API. You just made your first request!\n\n- Read the [API reference](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro)\n- Explore [examples](https://developers.notion.com/page/examples)"
}
```

```
// Save as quickstart.mjs after running: npm insta
...
` value and open it in your browser.
* **From Notion:** Look in **Private** in your sidebar for 🚀 **Hello from the API**.

Open the page and you should see your heading, paragraph, and bullet list inside.


Getting an error?

Error responses return a JSON object with a `code` and `message`:

```
{
  "object": "error",
  "status": 401,
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "API token is invalid."
}
```

| Error | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `unauthorized` | Double-check that your token is correct and hasn’t expired. |
| `validation_error` | Check the request body against the Create a page reference. |

For the full list of error codes, see Status codes.

## Next steps

Now that you’ve made your first request, explore what else you can build.

## Pages

Create, update, and retrieve page content.

## Databases

Create a database and find its data sources.

## Views

Create and configure database
...


## File uploads

Upload and attach files to pages and databases.

## Comments

Handle page and inline comments.

## Content queries

Find pages and data sources by title.

## Users

Read user profiles available to your connection.

For a team automation or an app others can install, compare connections and tokens.

## API reference

Browse every endpoint, request parameter, and response field.

### Connection permissions

Before a connection can interact with your Notion workspace page(s), the page must be manually shared with the connection. To share a page with a connection, visit the page in your Notion workspace, click the ••• menu at the top right of a page, scroll down to `Add connections`, and use the search bar to 
...

* The template is duplicated as a new page in the workspace.
* The new page is shared with the connection.

If the user chooses to select pages to share with the connection, then they continue to the page picker interface that’s part of the prompt for a standard connection.

After a user authorizes an OAuth integration, only that user is able to interact or share pages and databases with the connection. Unlike internal connections, if multiple members in a workspace want to use an OAuth integration, each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection.

**User authorization failures**
User authorization failures can happen. If a user chooses to `Cancel` the request, then a failure is triggered. Build your connection to handle these cases gracefully, as needed.
In some cases, Notion redirects the user to the `redirect_uri` that you set up when you created the OAuth integration, along with an `error` query parameter. When you first created the OAuth integration, you specified a redirect URI. If the user follows the prompt to `Allow access` for the connection, then Notion generates a temporary `code` and sends a request to the redirect URI with the following information in the query string:


| Parameter | Description | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | A temporary authorization code. | ✅ |
| `state` | The value provided by the connection when the user was prompted for access. |  |

To complete the next step, retrieve the `code` query parameter provided in the redirect. The retrieval method varies depending on your app’s tech stack.
In a React component, for example, the query parameters are made available through the `useRouter()` hook:

```
export default function AuthRedirectPage() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const { code } = router.query;
  ...
}
```

The connection needs to exchange the temporary `code` for an `access_token`.
To set up this step, retrieve the `code` from the redirect URI.
Next, send the `code` as part of a `POST` request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token.
This endpoint is described in more detail in the API reference docs for creating a token.
The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s `CLIENT_ID

## What is authorization?

Authorization is the process of granting a connection or token access to Notion data. Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token, personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

sources.title: Connect Notion to your AI assistant with MCP
sources.trimmed:
The easiest way to connect is through your AI assistant’s connector or plugin library. You can also browse available connections in Notion under **Settings** → **Notion MCP**.

## From your AI assistant

Find Notion in your assistant’s connector or plugin library.

## From Notion

Browse the directory in Notion’s settings.

## Manual setup

Add Notion MCP using a server URL or client configuration.

## Connect from your AI assistant

Open your AI assistant’s connector or plugin library and search for **Notion**. Select it and follow the prompts to authorize access to your Notion workspace.
After you authorize the connection, your AI assistant can read and update content that you can access in the selected workspace.
If Notion isn’t listed, check whether your assistant supports adding a custom MCP server and follow manual setup.

## Connect from Notion

In Notion, open **Settings** → **Notion MCP** and browse the directory. Select your AI assistant and follow its connection instructions.

## Manual setup

Use these instructions if you’re adding Notion as a custom MCP server or configuring a client directly. The remote server URL is `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`.

## Codex

## Claude Code

## Cursor

## fx

## Hermes

## Devin

## Pi

## VS Code

## Antigravity

## Other MCP clients

### Codex (ChatGPT)

Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent. See the Codex MCP documentation for more details.

Install the Codex CLI before running the commands below. If you see `command not found`, make sure `codex` is on your `PATH`.

1

Add the Notion server to your Codex configuration at `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```
[mcp_servers.notion]
url = "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp"
```

2

Authenticate by running:

```
codex mcp login notion
```

Complete the OAuth flow to connect your Notion workspace.

Project-level configuration

To share the Notion MCP configuration with your team, create a `.codex/config.toml` file in your project root with the same server configuration.
